parallel.requirements: Recognized the full Mootdx prompt and converted it into a spec checklist covering imports, constants, CLI, readers, quotes, financial data, cache, adjustment, demjson, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned the implementation, vendored upstream source, ran visible tests, then delegated a workflow audit over seven slices with second-phase verifier agents per returned finding.
parallel.implementation: Copied upstream mootdx and tests early, wrote package metadata and exports, later applied selected verifier-driven fixes including consts/check_empty, contrib adjust exports, and sample NUM_SAMPLES.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration occurred directly in the shared workspace by the parent while workflow children audited current files; final response was empty and the workflow aggregate was killed before a clean closure.
parallel.verification: Ran the visible upstream suite to 95 passed and 48 skipped, then reran after edits and saw 10 failures before the official evaluator reported 82 of 92 with solution_passed false.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Unfinished result reduction and post-merge verification remained at timeout; several confirmed audit items were not cleanly closed before official evaluation.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Mootdx project requirements and inspected package metadata, tdxpy internals, upstream source, tests, docs, sample files, and pyproject expectations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single parent without workflows, subagents, or delegation; it sequentially implemented files, compared with upstream, then replaced much of the tree with official source.
serial.implementation: Hand-built numerous modules at first, later copied the official source tree and wrote a setuptools-based pyproject to make the package importable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All writes were local to the parent trajectory; no child artifacts required joining, and the final response was empty after timeout.
serial.verification: Smoke-tested core imports successfully, but the later offline-capable pytest command ended with Exit code 137; official evaluation reported 78 of 92 with solution_passed false.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Sequential work timed out before broad verification and targeted fixes comparable to the parallel audit could be completed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the full Mootdx requirement set, built a spec checklist, and checked official-style imports, CLI, readers, quotes, financial, cache, adjustment, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt and eventually used upstream source and official tests as the target behavior while keeping all work local.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the broad library-building task; parallel spent extra effort transforming the prompt into a delegated audit checklist, while serial kept requirements in one sequential context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation but delegated broad audit slices and verifier checks through one workflow over seven slices plus per-finding verifier agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had workflows and delegation disabled and used no subagents; the parent owned all implementation, source copying, pyproject writing, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added a broad audit/verification hierarchy on top of parent edits; serial had a single owner and no coordination overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs identified /workspace, /tmp/spec_checklist.md, the relevant module slices, and repro requirements, so the retained issue is not a missing context or interface contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept task facts, source comparisons, and implementation choices inside one parent trajectory, avoiding child handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main contrast is not context loss: parallel transmitted sufficient slice context but created many reports to reduce, while serial avoided handoff reduction entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel vendored upstream early, adjusted package exports and pyproject, ran visible tests, then later applied verifier-driven fixes such as contrib adjust re-export and sample NUM_SAMPLES.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial first wrote many modules by hand, then replaced them with the official source tree, wrote a setuptools pyproject, and only smoke-tested before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a stronger implementation state earlier and applied some audit fixes; serial spent more of the run constructing and replacing the tree before broad validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the workflow, received many child findings and verifier verdicts through the journal, but the aggregate workflow state ended killed with a null result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its local smoke test returned successfully and the later offline test command was killed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a nontrivial result lifecycle and unfinished reduction of child results; serial had ordinary sequential command results only.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent edited the shared workspace while workflow children audited and some verifiers tested current files, but no independent same-file overwrite consequence was proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and copied files in one trajectory, with no live subagents and no concurrent workspace writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace coordination exposure, but the proved adverse consequence is budget exhaustion rather than a write collision; serial had no comparable concurrency boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first had 95 visible tests passing, then a later full rerun exposed 10 visible failures after edits, and the official evaluator recorded 82/92 with solution_passed false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial smoke-tested core imports successfully, then its offline-capable pytest command was killed before usable test output, and the official evaluator recorded 78/92 with solution_passed false.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed more explicit verification and scored higher, but neither run reached official acceptance; serial had less late verification before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 30 workflow child logs, 573 workflow-child tool calls, large child token volume, timed out, and had a killed workflow/empty final response at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with no delegation, no workflow tasks, and no child tokens; its final local action was a killed pytest command.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both ran out of time, but parallel spent a material closing window on broad fan-out and verifier reduction; serial exhaustion was from sequential implementation and testing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial both have solution_passed false. Parallel passed 82/92 while serial passed 78/92, indicating better coverage but not a pass/fail outcome difference. The concrete strategy difference is that parallel established an upstream-based baseline and used child audit/verifier results for some late fixes, while serial spent much of the run on sequential construction and copied upstream near the deadline. The retained parallel pattern is adverse process evidence, not an explanation for a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Early upstream vendoring and visible 95-passed baseline improved coverage.
Broad workflow audit found several concrete gaps and enabled selected late fixes.
Fan-out and retry breadth consumed the closing window, leaving reduction and final verification incomplete.
serial_contributors: Sequential implementation avoided child coordination overhead.
Late upstream source copy and pyproject write produced importable baseline but left little time for broader tests.
Final offline pytest command was killed before useful acceptance evidence could be produced.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel applied some spec-specific export and sample fixes that serial did not reach before timeout.
Both retained ordinary implementation/test gaps reflected by official failures; these are not all attributable to concurrency.
evaluator_effects: Outcome was resolved from current completed cell/status.json evaluation records, not stale aggregate fields.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process difference only

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parent implemented and edited the project directly; the workflow delegated audit and verification, not ownership-free implementation.
Rejected: the parent retained integration responsibility and made concrete edits; no separately owned component set lacked an integration owner.
Rejected: the workspace deliverable existed and the remaining problem was timeout/budget, not an unowned final artifact placement step.
Rejected: the parent owned the end-to-end build/test/edit loop; the pipeline was compressed by time rather than ownerless.
Rejected: visible implementation and tests occurred before the audit workflow; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory preflight gate.
Rejected: investigation/audit came after substantial implementation and overlapped with continued parent work; it was not a separate all-investigation phase before all production work.
Rejected: the adverse allocation is better and more specifically described as collective audit/verifier fan-out exhausting the finite closing budget.

The parallel workflow split the audit across seven slices and then launched a verifier agent for up to 24 findings per slice. The resulting workflow had 30 child logs, a recorded stall retry, killed status, and no aggregate result, while the parent was still reducing findings and applying fixes near timeout. This consumed closing time needed for result reduction, post-merge verification, and final closure; serial performed the same task sequentially without workflow fan-out.
candidates.realized_consequence: Killed audit workflow and exhausted closing budget left verifier findings only partially reduced and left final verification/closure incomplete.
candidates.near_match_reason: Missing Verifier Return is a symptom here: the aggregate workflow result was absent because the broad fan-out and retry chain exhausted the run window, so reducing fan-out is the corrective boundary.

Rejected: the visible retry kept the same finding context and is part of the fan-out/stall chain, not a replacement with missing inherited state that repeated prior work.
